objective: Confirm the browse MCP server, the screen tool grant and the setup checks add no privilege, supply-chain or data-exposure defect.
scope: Commit ec15538d on release/0.3.1/feat/screen in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-screen (range 3f1c135b..ec15538d), plus merges of the fff branch and the integration branch up to c6a2ac71; source diff without dist at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-holyagent/43946df6-456d-58c6-bea3-7e958fcb9495/scratchpad/screen-commit.diff; writer report /home/user/holyagent/.git/holyagent/reports/assignment-0mw9trshx-cnhq.md

Requirements: opencode browse is @opencode/browse (MIT, 0.0.15, stdio MCP server plus a paired Chromium extension driving the user's real browser), registered for Pi at an exact pin moved by deps:update; setup reports when the extension is not installed or paired. Computer use is not a role but a screen capability an Assignment can carry; it grants computer-use tools (pi-computer-use), browser use (opencode browse) and the T3 in-app browser (T3 preview tools where T3 hosts the session), and routes that Assignment to GPT-6.1 Terra whatever its role, at least medium. The screen capabilities are granted per Assignment to keep specialist tool lists small. Capabilities have headless and normal forms: the screen capability uses a headless Playwright Chromium in a cloud or CI session and the paired real browser and desktop computer use on a desktop; setup and doctor detect the system and pick the form, and a capability whose needs are missing is reported, not silently dropped. Everything is modular, can be turned off on its own, with exact pins moved by deps:update.

Known gaps from the writer to judge: no headless Playwright Chromium form was built (browse drives a real browser only); browse 0.0.16 exists, the pin stays at 0.0.15; a second agent file per specialist (<agent>-screen, 36 in all) carries the screen tools; the Claude host refuses screen Assignments; the R-SCREEN requirement was added to the requirements tree and all three families.
constraints: Read-only: no edits, no git writes. Run commands only in /home/user/holyagent-0.3.1-screen and pass the explicit range 3f1c135b..c6a2ac71 to any review command.
Read @opencode/browse 0.0.15 from npm where the integration's assumptions need checking.
Testing is unit tests and fixtures only: never start pi, a browser, the browse server or T3.
Report in under 450 words; start each evidence line with the exact criterion text, a colon and the support inline.

criteria.text: Only Assignments the root marks as screen get browser and computer control, and nothing in a repository or report can grant it
The browse server is pinned exactly and started only for screen specialists, with no token or pairing secret written or logged
Setup and doctor checks run no untrusted command and write nothing outside recorded settings

result:
result: no blocker found; the three criteria hold as written. I raised two non-blocking suspicions, one of them a repo-controlled `.npmrc` that could change which package `npx` fetches. I could not run the built-in `/security-review`, and I read the code without running any tests.

Coverage limits:
- **Built-in `/security-review`:** it failed with `fatal: ambiguous argument 'origin/HEAD...'` because `origin/HEAD` does not exist in `/home/user/holyagent`. I had no shell to fix that, so it covered nothing. I reviewed the diff file and the worktree sources instead.
- **No tests run:** I had no Bash tool.
- **npm package read:** I read only the registry metadata and `package.json` of 0.0.15, not its `dist` code. The metadata shows MIT, SLSA provenance, a GitHub trusted publisher, exact-pinned dependencies and no shrinkwrap.

blockers: none

notes (suspicions, not validated):
1. **`.npmrc` redirect (PLAUSIBLE).**
   - The server is `npx -y @opencode/browse@0.0.15 mcp`, registered with no cwd and no registry argument (`packages/runtime/src/config/capabilities.ts`).
   - npm reads `.npmrc` from the project directory, so a hostile repository's `.npmrc` could point the registry at its own host. It could also supply a local `node_modules` copy.
   - The attacker needs a repository the user opens and a screen specialist launched there. The impact is code execution as the user in a session that also holds browser and desktop control.
   - The exact version does not help, because npm only checks integrity against whatever registry it was pointed at. Suggested fix: pass `--registry=https://registry.npmjs.org/`.
   - I could not confirm that Pi starts the server in the project cwd, since I did not start Pi.
2. **Soft gate on Pi.**
   - The screen tools reach a specialist only through the `<agent>-screen` file. `refuseNonSpecialist` and the workflow check accept any `-screen` name without tying it to an Assignment.
   - Pi's `assignment record` passes no `launchedAs`, so an agent/Assignment mismatch is checked only in the Claude hook, which is bookkeeping.
   - The only fix is the root's instructions, and root-model steering (a prompt injected through a repository or report) could still launch a `-screen` agent directly.
   - This was already true for computer use on visual roles. It now covers all 18 roles, including reviewers.
3. **Confirmations off.** `confirmAppLaunch` and `confirmDangerousActions` are false (pre-existing), so a screen specialist drives the user's logged-in browser and desktop unprompted.
4. **Repo agent files.** The project's `.pi/agents` outranks the package's agent files. A repository `-screen.md` could replace the tool list or prompt, as it already could for the 18 base names, so this adds no new privilege.

evidence:
- Only Assignments the root marks as screen get browser and computer control, and nothing in a repository or report can grant it: holds, with note 2 as the caveat.
  - `screen` exists only in `AssignmentDraft`, which is strictly decoded and comes from the root, so a report cannot set it.
  - Browse tools are `screen`-only and excluded from the root (`tools.rootExclude`) and from non-screen roles (`visual: []`).
  - The Claude host refuses screen dispatch (`packages/runtime/src/cli/assignment.ts`).
- The browse server is pinned exactly and started only for screen specialists, with no token or pairing secret written or logged: holds, with note 1 as the caveat.
  - The pin is `"0.0.15"` in `pi-packages.json`.
  - `registerScreenServers` returns early unless `isScreenAgent(childAgent(sessionName))`, and the headless form and `browserUse: false` register none.
  - No `mcp.json` is written. The pairing token is validated but never copied into `PairedBrowser`.
  - Errors carry only the path and the OS message.
- Setup and doctor checks run no untrusted command and write nothing outside recorded settings: holds.
  - `reportBrowserUse` and `checkPairing` call `which` and read `browser-tokens.json` read-only.
  - They never run `npx` or browse. I read the diff and `pi-check.ts` for this and did not run the tests.
- findings: notes 1 to 4 above; no validated vulnerability.

acceptance.rationale: Review evidence holds; findings go to the repair
